title: The morphism from a line quotient by homogeneous fractions
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal E$ an arbitrary quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module [pqf-def-coherent], and $p:P=\operatorname{Proj}_S A_S(\mathcal E)\to S$, where $A_S(\mathcal E)$ is the canonical symmetric graded algebra [def-trf-canonical-symmetric-graded-algebra] and relative Proj is [def-nagata-relative-proj]. No finite-type or local-freeness hypothesis is imposed on $\mathcal E$. Let $h:T\to S$ be any scheme morphism, $L$ an invertible $\mathcal O_T$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], and $q:h^*\mathcal E\twoheadrightarrow L$ a surjective sheaf homomorphism, with tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. There is a unique graded algebra map $\psi:h^*A_S(\mathcal E)\to\bigoplus_{d\ge0}L^{\otimes d}$ whose degree-one part is $q$ and whose degree-zero part is the structural unit (tensor powers use [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]). For $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$, put $M=\mathcal E(U)$ and $A=\operatorname{Sym}_R M$. On each affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq h^{-1}U$ with a frame $l$ of $L$, write $q(m\otimes1)=b_m l$ under $(h^*\mathcal E)(W)=M\otimes_R B$. Write $b(a)$ for the coefficient of $l^{\otimes d}$ in $\psi(a)$ for $a\in A_d$. The opens $W_m=D(b_m)$ cover $W$, and for $e=\iota(m)$ the formula
$$\rho_m:(A_e)_0\longrightarrow B[1/b_m],\qquad a/e^d\longmapsto b(a)/b_m^d\quad(a\in A_d)$$
is a well-defined $R$-algebra homomorphism (degree-zero localization is [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero]). Its spectrum map sends $W_m$ into $D_+(e)\subset P$. These maps agree on overlaps, where for $f=\iota(n)$ the function $f/e$ maps to the unit $b_n/b_m$. Replacing $l$ by $u l$, $u\in B^\times$, replaces the degree-$d$ coefficients by $u^{-d}b(a)$ and leaves every $\rho_m$ unchanged; the same formulas commute with affine base restriction. The local maps determine a unique $S$-morphism $F_h(L,q):T\to P$ satisfying these formulas for every such $U,W,l,m$, independent of all these choices. The domain $U(\psi)$ is all of $T$ and $F_h(L,q)$ equals the canonical relative-Proj morphism $r_{L,\psi}$ of [lem-trf-space-line-module-proj-map].

proof.text: Use the section-normalized tensor-pullback adjunction to regard q as a map E→h_*L. For each affine base U, construct the commutative direct sum of sections of all tensor powers of L on h^(-1)(U), using the tensor-power associativity and local-frame commutativity identities. SymmetricAlgebra.lift sends a generator m to the degree-one section obtained from q by the inverse right unitor. Induction on powers of the generator range shows that degree n maps to the nth direct-sum component. Projecting gives a concrete graded extension. Scalar, product, unit and restriction identities follow by injectivity of each direct-sum inclusion and equality on scalars and generators. The right unitor proves that this extension recovers q.

proof.text: Induction on powers of the symmetric generator range proves uniqueness of the extension. Every tensor power of a frame is a free generator. Its scalar-multiplication bijection identifies the coefficient chosen by invFun. Apply the right unitor and the extension equation to identify degree-one coefficients with the quotient generator coefficients. Injectivity of scalar multiplication proves the frame-change, source-restriction and base-restriction identities.

source.place: Tags 01OA (section-projective-bundle), 01O4 (lemma-apply-relative), 01NA (lemma-apply), and 01O9 (lemma-invertible-map-into-relative-proj); graded extension and affine homogeneous-fraction construction.

proof.text: Tensor pullback preserves quasi-coherence. The affine surjectivity lemma in the quasi-coherent cokernel/image module lifts the frame through q on W. The tensor-pullback affine sections comparison lifts that section to a finite tensor sum. Tensor induction shows that its frame coefficient lies in the ideal generated by all quotient generator coefficients. Since this coefficient is 1, the ideal is the unit ideal and the basic opens cover W. On stalks a free frame remains a basis; the unit coefficient on one covering generator open shows that the homogeneous degree-one section is outside the maximal-ideal multiple. Thus the graded extension generates everywhere.

proof.text: Apply the general affine-basis homogeneous-fraction atlas to this graded extension and its frame coefficients. Specialize its denominator to the degree-one symmetric generator. This supplies the canonical morphism and all scalar, fraction and chart equations. On a double generator open, both coefficients are units; the localization equation for c/b proves that its image is a unit. Together with the already proved coefficient identities this is the full quotient chart predicate.

proof.text: For frame independence, scalar-preserving transports of two charts have the same source scheme morphism. Their composites with F therefore agree. Cancel the monomorphisms of the relative-Proj affine chart and its D_+(e) chart, then use faithfulness of Spec to obtain equality of ring maps. For uniqueness of F, the fraction formulas and homogeneous-fraction surjectivity identify the two chart ring maps. Their spectrum equations give equal restrictions to every generator open. The generator cover and local equality of scheme morphisms prove global equality.
